units.source_text: “工艺不精之辈的手艺，有什么不敢当的呢。

en.t: For the handiwork of someone unskilled in the craft, there is really nothing to be so deferential about.

units.source_text: 新年也快到了，画赤松和杉树还算合时。

en.t: The New Year is nearly here too, so painting red pines and cedars is still fitting for the season.

units.source_text: 我本来想把赤松放在后面结成鼓形，

en.t: At first I meant to put the red pines in the back and arrange them in the shape of a drum,

units.source_text: 可是千重子小姐却说应该把杉树放到后面。

en.t: but Miss Chieko said the cedars ought to be placed in the back instead.

units.source_text: 到这儿来，我才真正明白了。

en.t: Only after coming here did I truly understand.

units.source_text: 一听说杉树，就马上联想到它是一棵棵大树、老树，其实……

en.t: When one hears cedar, one immediately thinks of great old trees standing one after another, but in fact...

units.source_text: 我把它画得比较优雅一点，或许算是作品的特色吧。

en.t: I painted them a little more elegantly, and perhaps that may count as the distinctive quality of the work.

units.source_text: 还用了一些赤松的树干作陪衬……”

en.t: I also used some red pine trunks as a supporting accent..."
